_note: How each culture builds its towns, for worlds made since terrainGen 4 (world/townPlanner.js, world/cultures.js). `families` are the culture's own buildings, composed from the building kit (data/buildingKit.json kit) by scripts/compose-buildings.js into data/buildings.json with their culture stamped on (a family with buildingTypes makes each of those types: halls, trades, workshops). `mix` is which house styles stand where (core: the middle of town, mid, edge: the outskirts). `plan` is the town's shape: straight or winding streets (wind), lanes close or far apart (laneGap), houses shoulder to shoulder or apart (gap, setback), the square (plaza: square, green or long; its centre piece and corner pieces, stall count), how the streets are surfaced (streets: the top-left cell of a 2x2 block of streetSheet, painted by scripts/terrain_modern/build_streets.py, or none for dirt tracks), lamps (none, square, street, all), props along the streets, and things standing about town (scatter). `interior` is what their houses are made of inside (data/innerMapRenderer.json interiorArt).

Imperial.summary: Red brick and terracotta in a grid of straight streets; a great paved square with a fountain and columns, lamp posts everywhere, rows of tall townhouses shoulder to shoulder.

Religious.summary: Pale limestone and whitewash under slate, arched double doors and pointed windows; a cloister-like square of cream flagstones round a white column, planters and a calm grid of streets with gardens.

Arcane.summary: Dark stone and grey brick under violet shingles and verdigris tiles, tall ornate windows lit at all hours; dark slate streets lined with lamp posts on every lane, a black obelisk in the square.

Woodland.summary: Black-and-white timber framing and golden thatch, flower boxes and porches; winding dirt lanes, cottages set apart in their gardens, oaks left standing in town and a village green with a great oak instead of a paved square.

Swamp.summary: Low huts of tarred and weathered boards under dark, mossy thatch; few windows, crooked dirt paths wandering between scattered homes, a well and a fire in a trampled clearing, trees crowding in.

Nordic.summary: Long low halls of Falu-red and tarred log siding under green turf roofs, carved rune-stones; dirt lanes bending round a village green with a rune-stone, pines between the houses.

Mountain.summary: Squat, thick-walled houses of fieldstone and dark granite under heavy slate, few small windows; a tight, walled-in huddle with narrow straight lanes paved in dark flags, a deep stone well in a small square.

Nomadic.summary: Low mud-brick houses with flat roofs and brown tile; dusty unpaved tracks, homes spread wide apart, and a long open bazaar street crowded with stalls instead of a square.

Desert.summary: Whitewashed and sand-coloured adobe with flat parapet roofs, carved lattice and pointed windows, arched double doors; houses packed wall to wall along sandy lanes, a great bazaar square round a pool with a date palm at each corner, potted trees along the lanes and palms standing about the town.

Maritime.summary: Clapboard and plaster houses painted blue, teal, yellow, white and rose under blue slate; one long cobbled harbour street with a market strung along it, lamps, barrels and crates at every door.
